steps.title: Collect conditioned medium
steps.instruction: Culture KW10 glioma cells in DMEM/F12 containing 10 % EV‑depleted FBS for 48–72 h, then collect the conditioned medium (CM).

steps.title: Process conditioned medium
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the CM at 800 × g for 10 min at 4 °C in a swinging‑bucket rotor, filter the supernatant through a 0.45 µm syringe filter, and store at –80 °C (up to 1–2 months) or at 4 °C for immediate use.

steps.title: Isolate EVs by PEG precipitation
steps.instruction: Prepare 20 % (w/v) PEG10000 solution in deionized water filtered through a 0.22 µm membrane. Mix 5 ml of CM with 5 ml of the 20 % PEG10000 solution, invert the tube 10 times, incubate on ice for 1 h, then centrifuge at 3000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C. Decant the supernatant carefully, centrifuge the tube again at 3000 × g for 5 min to remove residual liquid, and dissolve the resulting pellet in 200 µl PBS (transfer to a fresh 1.5 ml micro‑centrifuge tube).

steps.title: Permeabilize EVs
steps.instruction: Add Triton X‑100 to a final concentration of 0.001 % (v/v) to the EV suspension and incubate for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Add PEG and spin
steps.instruction: Add PEG10000 to reach a final concentration of 10 % (no incubation required), then spin the suspension at 3000 × g for 5 min at room temperature. Carefully remove the supernatant and dissolve the pellet in 100 µl PBS.

steps.title: Add primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Add primary antibodies against TSG101, CD63, and calnexin to a final concentration of 0.01 µg/µl (i.e., 1 µg of each antibody per 100 µl EV suspension). Incubate the mixture for 90 min with gentle shaking at room temperature.

steps.title: PEG precipitation to remove primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of 20 % PEG10000 solution to the antibody‑EV mixture, centrifuge at 3000 × g for 5 min, and resuspend the pellet in 100 µl PBS. Repeat this PEG precipitation step two additional times (total three precipitations) to eliminate excess primary antibodies.

steps.title: Add secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Add Alexa Fluor‑labeled species‑specific secondary antibodies (Invitrogen catalog numbers A11005 and A11012) diluted 1:100 to the EV suspension. Incubate for 1 h with gentle shaking in the dark at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash unbound secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Wash the EV‑antibody complex three times with PEG10000 by centrifuging at 3000 × g (same speed as step 4) and discarding the supernatant each time. After the final wash, dissolve the pellet in 100 µl PBS.

steps.title: Purify via Sephadex G‑25 column
steps.instruction: Pass the EV suspension through a Sephadex G‑25 column (Sigma G2580) to remove unbound antibodies and antibody‑antigen complexes. Collect the flow‑through, add PEG solution (as in step 4) to precipitate the EVs, centrifuge at 3000 × g for 5 min, discard the supernatant, and dissolve the final pellet in 20 µl PBS.

steps.title: Prepare microscopy slides
steps.instruction: Place 3–4 µl of the labeled EV suspension on a pre‑cleaned microscope slide, spread a thin smear with a coverslip, and let the slide dry in the dark for 5–10 min before imaging.

steps.title: Image labeled EVs
steps.instruction: Analyze the prepared slides using confocal or STED microscopy (Leica TCS SP8 STED 3X). For dSTORM imaging, use anti‑mouse Alexa 488 (Invitrogen A11001) or Alexa 555 (Invitrogen A21422) secondary antibodies as indicated.

steps.title: Optional gold labeling for TEM
steps.instruction: Replace Alexa Fluor secondary antibodies with gold‑conjugated secondary antibodies (anti‑mouse gold IgG, Sigma G7527; anti‑rabbit gold IgG, Sigma G7402) and follow the same immune‑staining protocol. After labeling, stain the samples with uranyl acetate as described for TEM preparation.
